seo.howTo: How to use this PDF tool
seo.privacy: Paperwork processes PDFs in your browser, without uploading your documents. No account or payment is required. Download the result to keep your changes, and keep a copy of your original. Large documents may take longer or exceed your device’s available memory.
seo.workspacePlaceholder: Enable JavaScript to choose a PDF and use the tool. Your documents are processed on your device. Instructions are below.
seo.notFoundDescription: This page doesn’t exist. Browse the PDF tools to find what you need.

toImages.step1: Choose the PDF you want to convert.
toImages.step2: Pick PNG or JPG, a resolution, and which pages to export.
toImages.step3: Download the image, or a ZIP file when you export several pages.
toImages.limitation: Each page becomes a flat picture, so text in the images can’t be selected. Very large pages are scaled down to fit your browser’s limits.

fromImages.step1: Choose the images you want in your PDF, such as photos or scans.
fromImages.step2: Drag them into order, then pick a page size and margin.
fromImages.step3: Create the PDF and download it, or continue in another tool.
fromImages.limitation: Each image becomes one page, and text in the images can’t be selected or searched. Formats your browser can’t open, such as HEIC outside Safari, need converting first.

merge.step1: Choose the PDF files you want to combine.
merge.step2: Drag the files into the order you want in the final document.
merge.step3: Merge the files and download the combined PDF.
merge.limitation: Unlock password-protected files before merging. Check the page order in your downloaded document.

split.step1: Choose the PDF you want to split.
split.step2: Extract page ranges, split into fixed-size chunks, or create one file per page.
split.step3: Download the extracted PDF or the archive of split files.
split.limitation: Page numbers start at 1. Use ranges such as 1-3, 5, 8- to select pages; they must exist in the document.

compress.step1: Choose the PDF whose file size you want to reduce.
compress.step2: Choose light, medium, or strong compression and run it.
compress.step3: Compare the resulting size and download the smaller PDF when available.
compress.limitation: Some PDFs are already optimized and won’t get smaller. Strong compression turns pages into images, which removes selectable text and may reduce visual quality.

sign.step1: Choose a PDF, then draw, type, or import your signature.
sign.step2: Place and resize the signature on the page where it belongs.
sign.step3: Download the signed PDF and check the signature placement.
sign.limitation: This adds a visible signature, not a certificate-based digital signature. Check the recipient’s signing requirements before using it.

annotate.step1: Choose a PDF and navigate to the page you want to annotate.
annotate.step2: Add text, highlights, notes, or shapes, and adjust their placement.
annotate.step3: Download the annotated PDF to save your additions.
annotate.limitation: Annotations add to the document; they don’t edit its original text. Use the redaction tool to remove sensitive text instead of covering it with a shape.

organize.step1: Choose the PDF whose pages you want to arrange.
organize.step2: Reorder, rotate, or remove pages using the page thumbnails.
organize.step3: Download the reorganized PDF and review its page order.
organize.limitation: Keep at least one page in the document. Removing a page from the output doesn’t change your original file.

security.step1: Choose unlock, protect or remove hidden information, then select your PDF.
security.step2: Enter the current password when required. To protect a file, enter and confirm a new password.
security.step3: Process the document and download the resulting PDF.
security.limitation: Unlocking requires the password when the document needs one; this tool doesn’t recover forgotten passwords. Keep any new password somewhere safe.

redact.step1: Choose a PDF and open the page containing sensitive text.
redact.step2: Select the text you want to remove and review the marked areas.
redact.step3: Download the redacted PDF and check it before sharing.
redact.limitation: This tool supports text redaction and rejects areas that overlap images. It isn’t suitable for removing information from scanned images. Review every page for other sensitive content.

watermark.step1: Choose a PDF and enter the text for your watermark.
watermark.step2: Adjust its appearance and choose the pages to watermark.
watermark.step3: Apply the watermark and download the result.
watermark.limitation: A watermark adds visible text; it doesn’t prevent copying or remove the underlying content. Use redaction for supported sensitive text.

pageNumbers.step1: Choose the PDF you want to number.
pageNumbers.step2: Choose the number format, position, starting number, and page range.
pageNumbers.step3: Apply the numbering and download your PDF.
pageNumbers.limitation: New numbers are added over the page content. They don’t replace existing page numbers, so check their placement before sharing.

about.title: It started with an ID card.
about.intro: My girlfriend asked me to sign a copy of my ID card. Somehow, I ended up building an entire web app.
about.context: She needed the copy to handle some paperwork for me. I already kept a PDF in Google Drive, so it should have been easy. In Thailand, we often write a note across an ID copy saying what it can be used for, then sign it. All I needed was a few words in Thai and a signature.
about.problem: But the online PDF tools I tried either struggled with Thai characters or put what I needed behind limits and subscriptions. I switched between websites and my phone until I finally got it done. It took far longer than a single document should.
about.girlfriend: When I asked my girlfriend how she usually did it, she said it was easy. Then she tried, ran into the same limitations, and couldn’t finish it either. We had to laugh.
about.question: Why should an everyday task mean learning new software or paying for a monthly subscription?
about.solution: So I built Paperwork: simple, free tools for everyday PDF jobs. Add text, including Thai, sign a document, merge or split files, and rearrange pages, right in your browser. No sign-up, and your documents stay on your device. I built it for myself first, and wanted other people to be able to use it too.
about.invitation: If a supposedly simple PDF task has ever taken up too much of your day, tell me about it. It might be the next thing I build.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.subtitle: What’s new in Paperwork, newest first.

items.clear: Annotate has a Clear button in the toolbar. Clear the current page or every page at once, and undo it if you change your mind.

items.fonts: Choose Sans, Serif, Mono or Handwriting for text watermarks. Serif and Handwriting support Thai as well as Latin text; other scripts use a supported fallback font.
items.controls: Choose S, M, L or XL text, preset angles and opacity, and color swatches. Select Custom for precise values or your own color. Controls are easier to tap on mobile and more compact on desktop.

items.updates: Paperwork checks for new versions when you reopen the app or reconnect, and shows an Update now button. Download your work before updating, or choose Later to keep working.

items.privacy: A privacy page explains what Paperwork keeps on your device, with a button to clear it.
items.clean: Remove hidden information, such as properties, metadata, bookmarks and attachments, in Unlock and protect.
items.redact: Redaction also removes hidden information that can repeat the redacted text.
items.autosave: Autosaved annotations are deleted after 7 days.
items.security: A stricter security policy stops the app from sending your data to other sites.

items.imagesToPdf: Turn photos and scans into a PDF, one page per image, on A4, Letter or pages the size of each image.

workflows.title: More ways to work with PDFs

items.languages: Use Paperwork in Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Vietnamese and Spanish, alongside English and Thai.
items.images: Export PDF pages as PNG or JPG images, with a choice of resolution and page range.
items.files: Open PDFs from your device or share them to the installed app in supported browsers, then choose a tool.
items.continue: Send a finished PDF straight to another tool with Continue in….
items.signatures: Saved signatures, initials and stamps stay on your device and are available in both Sign and Annotate.
items.redact: Find and redact every match of text, a pattern or a common number format.
items.compress: Compression runs in the background, with custom image size and JPEG quality settings.
items.organize: Insert blank pages or another PDF, and duplicate pages in Organize.
items.merge: Merged PDFs keep their bookmarks and metadata.
items.changelog: Follow new features and improvements on the public changelog page.

items.install: Install Paperwork on your phone or computer and keep using the tools without a connection.
items.pricing: A pricing page, if you’re curious. It’s a short read.
items.previews: Links to Paperwork now show a proper preview when you share them.
items.prerender: Pages appear instantly and can be read by search engines, even before the app finishes loading.

items.redact: Redact sensitive text from a PDF so it’s gone for good, not just covered up.
items.security: Add a password to a PDF, or remove one you already know.
items.feedback: Send feedback straight from the app, in English or Thai.
items.about: An About page with the story of how Paperwork started.
items.preload: Tools open faster. Paperwork loads them quietly in the background while you browse.

items.tools: Eight PDF tools: merge, split, compress, organize, page numbers, watermark, sign and annotate.
items.thai: Proper Thai text support when you add text to a document, plus an English and Thai interface.
items.private: Everything runs in your browser. No sign-up, and your files never leave your device.

privacy.title: Your files stay on your device
privacy.intro: Paperwork has no accounts, analytics or ads. Here's what happens to your data.

files.title: Your PDFs and images
files.body: Every tool runs inside your browser. Your files are never uploaded, and the site's security policy stops the app from sending data anywhere except Paperwork itself.

stored.title: What's saved on this device
stored.body: Signatures, initials and stamps you choose to keep, annotations you're working on (deleted after 7 days), and your theme and language. They're stored only in this browser.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.body: If you send feedback, your message is forwarded to the developer through Discord. Don't include personal information. Your IP address is used briefly to limit how many messages can be sent.

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.body: Paperwork is hosted on Cloudflare, which handles standard request information such as your IP address to deliver the site and protect it from abuse.

clear.title: Clear local data
clear.body: Delete saved signatures, autosaved annotations and settings from this browser. This can't be undone.
